subject: scripts/schedule.py (actl schedule plan|run): DAG from tickets' depends_on + board/batches.json edited by main; dispatches auto-fix.sh up to schedule.max_workers, lands each all-green batch with land.sh t<a> t<b> …, wakes main only at terminal states; ticket.py lint rejects depends_on cycles
objective: User (2026-10-25): 「票的 DAG 應該可以跟 land.sh 1 2 3 連動…land.sh t162 t164 t165 應該是系統自動知道的,不是 llm 去控制的…LLM 應該是依我的要求去改 dag 的 batch 檔案,後面的 land 該怎麼跑應該是自動的」「開題者要在開題時把自己的票插入 dag」. D-073 ② (batch landing), D-067 (no polling; wake main only at terminal states), D-049 ④ (DAG). Main's batch-landing incidents 2026-10-25 (added by the opener on main's request): batch land t162+t164 merge-conflicted in bin/actl, scripts/gate.sh, tests/test_actl.py (#164 was started while #162 was not landed; #162 deleted gate.sh map() rows that #164 added to) -> (9); #162 landed alone went red 1 case, land.sh's own auto-fix round 2 went green + review pass, yet land.sh exited rc 1 and main re-ran land by hand -> (10); the container restarted / the 2 h background limit cut a driver on 2026-10-24 and 2026-10-25 -> (11). Rewritten after the subtraction audit (D-054): no queue platform, no PlanningBatch manifest, no slot API - one script over facts that already exist (ticket files, git, auto-fix.sh, land.sh, inbox.py). (1) scripts/schedule.py with 'plan' (read-only) and 'run'; bin/actl TABLE row 'schedule' and the case that execs it. (2) DAG: nodes = tickets in tickets_dir, edges = depends_on. A dependency is satisfied iff the dependency ticket is Done AND its landed_sha is an ancestor of main (git merge-base --is-ancestor) - 'Done' alone or a non-empty sha alone is not enough. Condition 'landed' (and legacy '落地…' / '已落地…' on Done tickets) is the only understood condition; any other string, a missing ticket, or a Cancelled/Blocked dependency -> the dependant is 'waiting(<reason>)', never dispatched, reason printed. A cycle or self-dependency among tickets that are not Done/Cancelled -> rc 2 naming the cycle; nothing starts. (3) Batch file board/batches.json, edited by main on the user's request: {"schema": 1, "batches": [{"id": "b1", "tickets": ["162", "164", "165"]}, {"id": "b2", "tickets": ["163", "166"]}, {"id": "b3", "tickets": ["167"]}]} - list order is landing order. Validation (rc 2, naming ticket / dependency / batch): unknown id, an id listed twice, invalid JSON, schema != 1, a dependency inside the same batch (gates are measured against main, not against a batch-mate), a dependency in a later batch or in no batch and not landed. Tickets not listed are untouched by run and printed under 'unscheduled'. File absent -> default plan: batch = every Ready ticket whose dependencies are all landed; after it lands, recompute (next frontier) until nothing is Ready or the frontier is empty while tickets wait (then stop and list why). (4) run, per batch: tickets already green (InReview, gate pass; complex also review.verdict pass per ticket.py review_problems) count as green without dispatch; Ready tickets get 'sh $AC_HOME/scripts/auto-fix.sh <n>' spawned (cwd AC_ROOT) with at most schedule.max_workers (board/config.json, default 2; one auto-fix = one worker + at most one verifier, 4 CPUs) running at once; the script blocks on its children (subprocess wait) - nobody polls status files. auto-fix rc 0 -> green. Any other rc -> that ticket is red-terminal for this run (auto-fix already wrote its own decision page): running children finish, no new dispatch in this batch, then stop (6). A ticket that is Running / InReview-without-gate at start -> rc 2 before anything starts ('another driver has #n') - except an orphan of this run's own state file, rule (11); complex InReview without a review verdict -> 'waiting(review)', counted not green, and if nothing else can move the run stops with a decision page naming review.sh. (5) All tickets of the batch green -> foreground 'sh $AC_HOME/scripts/land.sh <branch…>' (branch = ticket's branch field, else t<n>; batch-file order). land rc 0 -> land closed the tickets -> recompute, next batch. land rc != 0 -> rule (10) decides re-land or stop (land did its batch_fix / auto-fix and pages itself). (6) Terminal states, exactly one inbox page per run: every listed batch landed -> kind done, attached to the last landed ticket, listing batches and landed shas; any stop -> kind decision attached to the ticket that stopped it: what happened, what main does next (handle that ticket's page / edit board/batches.json / run review.sh), and 'actl schedule run' to resume. Nothing to dispatch or land at start -> rc 3, reasons on stdout, no page (DISPATCH-TEMPLATE §5.5: 'nothing to do' must not look like 'done'). Events: schedule.start (kv run_id, batches, max_workers), schedule.dispatch per ticket, schedule.land per batch (kv branches), schedule.stop (kv reason). Log: reports/schedule/<run_id>/schedule.log + plan.json. (7) Facts first: run recomputes from ticket files and git at start and after every land; the state file of (11) only carries what facts cannot answer (run_id, which children this run spawned, pre-land branch heads, re-land counts). Lock .schedule.lock (mkdir, like land's; holder file 'pid=<n> boot_id=<id> run_id=<r>') -> second run rc 2 naming the holder, unless the holder is stale (11). The scheduler never signals a child (no kill of any spelling): auto-fix and land own their timeouts. (8) 'ticket.py lint <n>' gains: depends_on cycle / self-dependency across tickets_dir -> rc 1 line 'depends_on cycle: a -> b -> a'; a condition other than 'landed' on the linted ticket -> rc 1 naming it; lint stays read-only. This is how an opener 'inserts a ticket into the DAG': write depends_on, run lint. (9) File overlap: files(t) = 'git diff --name-only <main_branch>...<branch>' for a ticket whose branch exists; no branch -> files unknown (printed 'files unknown', never read as 'no overlap'). Two tickets overlap iff their known file sets intersect. Never in the same land call: when a batch is all green, it is split in batch order into land calls - a ticket goes into the first call that holds no ticket it overlaps; each later call runs only after the previous landed (land rc 0). Dispatch: a Ready ticket whose branch already exists and overlaps an earlier batch-mate that is not landed is 'waiting(overlap #Y)' and dispatched only after #Y lands (it then builds on #Y). 'plan' prints one line per overlapping pair: 'overlap: #A #G (f1, f2) -> #G after #A'. A later call that merge-conflicts (land rc 3) -> stop, decision page naming that ticket, the earlier one and the overlapping files. Same rule with and without board/batches.json; batches.json is not refused for overlap (overlap is only measurable once branches exist). (10) Re-land after land's own fix: after a land call returns rc != 0 the scheduler re-reads the facts. Tickets of that call now Done with landed_sha on main count as landed (batch_fix may have re-landed some). The others are 'fixed' iff InReview, gate.rc 0, gate.sha == 'git rev-parse <branch>' now, that head differs from the head the scheduler recorded for that branch just before the land call (a new commit was gated - not the same red tree again), and complex -> review_problems empty. All not-landed tickets of the call fixed -> run land again on exactly those branches (same order), event schedule.land kv reland=<k>; at most schedule.reland_max (board/config.json, default 2) re-lands per batch per run; otherwise, or any ticket not fixed -> stop, decision page naming the ticket(s), the land rc and (if the cap was hit) 'reland_max'. (11) Scheduler state file reports/schedule/state.json (schema 1: run_id, pid, boot_id = /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id, started, batches [{id, tickets, status pending|dispatching|landing|landed|stopped, pre_land_heads {branch: sha}, relands}], children {ticket: {pid, boot_id, started}}, stop null | {reason, at}), rewritten atomically (temp file + os.replace) before every spawn, after every child exit, before and after every land call, and at stop. 'run' with a state.json whose stop is null resumes that run_id (event schedule.resume kv run_id; log appended to reports/schedule/<run_id>/schedule.log); facts still win (a batch whose tickets are Done on main is landed whatever status says). A Running ticket listed in state.children whose pid is gone (/proc/<pid> absent) or whose boot_id differs from now is an orphan of this run, not another driver: 'sh $AC_HOME/scripts/auto-fix.sh <n>' is spawned again (auto-fix continues from its own status file; its rc is handled as in (4)). A Running ticket not in state.children stays rc 2 'another driver'. A batch found in status landing: tickets landed -> landed; .land.lock present -> stop, page naming .land.lock (the scheduler never removes land's lock); else land again (counts as one re-land). At a terminal state stop is set; the next run moves state.json to reports/schedule/<old run_id>/state.json and starts a new run_id. Stale .schedule.lock (holder pid gone, or holder boot_id != current boot_id) -> taken over, stdout 'stale .schedule.lock (pid <n>) taken over'; a holder file without boot_id is judged by pid only. Liveness via /proc only - no signal-0 probe (hard_block). Not here: a board view of the plan (plan's stdout is the view), PlanningBatch manifests (#118), session registry / slot API (#117), write scopes (D-054 Q2; (9) measures overlap from the branches' actual diffs, not from declared scopes), resolving a merge conflict (stays a decision page), changing land.sh's own rc or its auto-fix path (the scheduler reads the facts after it), Controller (#120).

Facts at base 1b6ac4e: no script reads depends_on today (grep: only board.py renders it); land.sh maps branch t<n>[-…] -> ticket (376-390), refuses 0 commits / stale base_sha / hard_block / complex without review (ticket.py review_problems, objection_problems), takes .land.lock by mkdir (90-110), runs batch_fix itself and writes its own decision pages; auto-fix.sh <n> starts round 1 for a Ready ticket, rc table in its header (0 green incl. review pass; 1/3/4/5/6/7/8/9/10 stops) and writes decision pages for its stops; inbox.py post kinds are decision / done only (INBOX_KINDS); ticket.py lint 1664-1681 only checks tags (no cycle check) - add one; depends_on conditions in the ticket store: 50 'landed' (all open tickets), legacy '落地…' / '已落地…' / '' / 'stacked:…' only on Done/Cancelled tickets; states IntegrationQueued / Integrating exist in STATES but no script sets them (not used here either - land owns state). Measured here: gate.sh --base 35.5 s. #162 landed (654d419), so the dependency is satisfied; base moved to main head 3c81c2b (tickets-only commit on top). Judgement on the former prerequisites: #101 Done (its write-scope hints were later deleted by D-054 Q2; dependency dropped as satisfied-and-irrelevant); #117 (session registry v2, slot API) dropped from depends_on - the only thing #119 needed from it was a process slot, and a counter over the scheduler's own children is that; recommend keeping #117 Draft for the main to decide with its cluster (#120/#123/#124/#125), not a #119 matter; #118 (PlanningBatch manifest) recommend Cancel: superseded by this ticket's rule 'opener writes depends_on + lint checks cycles' and by board/batches.json for ordering - the user's words put the DAG in the tickets, not in a manifest. #93 stays frozen on #119 landing (D-050 ④) - unchanged. test_plan: Layers: unit (tests/test_schedule.py, harness Sandbox with the per-test ac-home copy whose auto-fix.sh / land.sh / review.sh are replaced by recording fakes, as test_land does with gate_stub; oracles are the fakes' call logs, the ticket files the fakes write and hand-written expected strings - never schedule.py's own output parsed back), unit (tests/test_ticket.py for lint), static/dogfood A8. Worker, foreground: timeout 590 python3 -m unittest tests.test_schedule; then tests.test_ticket; then tests.test_actl (TABLE row) and the base command once. Verifier (needs_verifier true, interface_fixed true: subcommands, batches.json schema 1, rc table 0/1/2/3, event names, page kinds and config key are pinned here) writes tests/test_schedule_cases.py in parallel: a Done dependency whose landed_sha is NOT an ancestor of main is not satisfied (the 'Done alone is not enough' rule, old A3); a batch whose land fails must not let a later batch's dependant dispatch; a ticket with legacy '落地(…)' condition on a Done dependency is dispatched; max_workers absent -> 2 (overlap == 2 with 3 tickets); two runs started together -> exactly one proceeds (lock); overlap is symmetric and computed against main, not against the batch-mate (tG changed f2, tA deleted f2 -> still overlap); a ticket with no branch never reads as 'no overlap' in plan output; a re-land never runs when any ticket of the failed call is Blocked; state.json is valid JSON at every snapshot (a fake auto-fix reads it mid-run) - no half-written file; schedule.reland_max absent -> 2. Mutations (not measured by opener): m1 as A4; m2 'Done' accepted without ancestry -> A1 J arm red; m3 max_workers ignored -> A3 overlap red; m4 cycle check removed -> A1 and A7 red; m5 lock ignored -> A6 red; m6 page written on rc 3 -> A5 last arm red; m7 overlap ignored (whole batch in one land call) -> A9 argv red; m8 no re-land after land rc 1 -> A10 first arm red; m9 pre-land head not compared (re-land on same head) -> A10 same-head arm red; m10 state.json written only at stop -> A11 snapshot arm red; m11 orphan treated as another driver -> A11 resume arm red; m12 stale lock not taken over -> A6 stale arms red. Timing margins: fakes sleep 2 s, overlap computed from epoch pairs. Container is uid 0; hard_block.patterns forbids os.kill / killpg / pkill / 'kill -' in added tests/** lines and the scheduler itself never signals children (A8 grep). Liveness of pids and lock holders is read from /proc/<pid> and /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id; the tests fake 'another boot' by writing a different boot_id into the state / lock file, never by signalling.
feature: agent-control: DAG scheduling and batch landing

interface_contracts.cli: actl schedule plan | run; plan is read-only (no spawn, no page, no event); run rc 0 all batches landed / 1 stopped (page written) / 2 refused before start (cycle, batch file, lock, Running ticket) / 3 nothing to do (no page).
interface_contracts.batch_file: board/batches.json {schema:1, batches:[{id, tickets:[ticket ids as strings]}]}; list order = landing order; absent = frontier default.
interface_contracts.config: board/config.json schedule.max_workers int >= 1, default 2 (one auto-fix.sh child = one slot); schedule.reland_max int >= 0, default 2 (re-lands per batch per run, rule 10).
interface_contracts.satisfied_dependency: dependency ticket state Done AND landed_sha is an ancestor of main_branch; condition 'landed' (legacy '落地…'/'已落地…' read as landed on Done tickets); anything else = waiting, printed.
interface_contracts.children: sh $AC_HOME/scripts/auto-fix.sh <n> and sh $AC_HOME/scripts/land.sh <branches>, cwd AC_ROOT, waited on; never signalled.
interface_contracts.events_pages: schedule.start / schedule.resume / schedule.dispatch / schedule.land (kv branches, reland) / schedule.stop (kv reason done|red|conflict|land|review|...); one inbox page per run (done or decision), none on rc 2/3.
interface_contracts.overlap: files(t) = git diff --name-only <main_branch>...<branch>; no branch = unknown, printed; overlapping tickets never share a land call, the later (batch order) lands in a later call; an existing-branch Ready ticket overlapping an un-landed earlier batch-mate waits for it.
interface_contracts.state_file: reports/schedule/state.json schema 1 {run_id, pid, boot_id, started, batches[{id, tickets, status, pre_land_heads, relands}], children{ticket:{pid, boot_id, started}}, stop}; atomic rewrite at every transition; stop null = resumable; liveness via /proc, never a signal.
interface_contracts.lock: .schedule.lock (mkdir) holder 'pid=<n> boot_id=<id> run_id=<r>'; stale (pid gone or other boot) -> taken over and printed; live -> rc 2.
